name: Biomedical KG Negative Statements Benchmarks
description: Knowledge graphs represent facts about real-world entities. Most of these facts are defined as positive statements. The negative statements are scarce but highly relevant under the open-world assumption. Furthermore, they have been demonstrated to improve the performance of several applications, namely in the biomedical domain. However, no benchmark dataset supports the evaluation of the methods that consider these negative statements. We present a collection of datasets for three relation prediction tasks - protein-protein interaction prediction, gene-disease association prediction and disease prediction - that aim at circumventing the difficulties in building benchmarks for knowledge graphs with negative statements. These datasets include data from two successful biomedical ontologies, Gene Ontology and Human Phenotype Ontology, enriched with negative statements. reputation: A niche biomedical knowledge-graph benchmark collection that is mainly used in the specific subcommunity studying negative statements and open-world relation prediction.
notes: Specialized biomedical KG datasets with negative statements; likely small and task-specific, with results depending on ontology-derived splits and embedding baselines rather than large-scale LLM evaluation.
